label: Espresso, one variable at a time
blurb: Taste and repeatability make the numbers useful. These paths explore the cup, rather than a shopping list of machines.

nodes.label: Dialling in by taste
nodes.blurb: Change one brewing variable and compare the result. Notes connect what you did with what you actually enjoyed in the cup.

nodes.label: Puck preparation
nodes.blurb: Distribution and a repeatable routine before brewing. The useful goal is consistency between cups, not an elaborate ritual for its own sake.

nodes.label: Comparative tasting
nodes.blurb: Compare two cups and describe the difference in your own words. Sweetness, texture, and finish are more useful than guessing a flavour correctly.

nodes.label: Milk drinks
nodes.blurb: The balance between coffee, milk, and texture. A familiar drink becomes a way to notice how the ingredients change one another.

nodes.label: A brew journal
nodes.blurb: Dose, output, beans, and a short tasting note. Keep only the details that help you repeat a cup you liked.

nodes.label: Exploring coffee origins
nodes.blurb: Compare coffees while keeping your routine familiar. Origin, processing, and roast become questions you can investigate through taste.
